utility.name: Xcel Energy (Public Service Company of Colorado)

requirements.item: Install an electric heavy-duty lever bypass (HDLB) meter socket per Xcel Energy Blue Book Section 4.11
requirements.quote: An electric heavy-duty lever bypass (HDLB) meter socket is installed. Please see section 4.11 Meter Socket in the Xcel Energy Standards of Installation and Use Manual.

requirements.item: Public authority must submit an approved inspection certificate to Xcel Energy Builders Call Line before meter set
requirements.quote: Prior to the scheduling of your meter installation, Xcel Energy must receive an approved inspection certificate.

requirements.item: Submit DER interconnection application online with Site Plan and Line Diagram; inverter must be UL 1741 certified
requirements.quote: ALL INVERTER EQUIPMENT MUST BE UL. 1741 CERTIFIED

open_questions: No Denver-specific residential electrical load calculation worksheet, required NEC 220 method (220.82 vs. 220.83), or EV charger load factor was found on denvergov.org; confirm directly with Denver CPD (planreview@denvergov.org) whether any load calculation documentation is requested at inspection or during E-permits submittal for single-family electrical permits.

Neither the Quick Permits page (https://www.denvergov.org/Government/Agencies-Departments-Offices/Agencies-Departments-Offices-Directory/Community-Planning-and-Development/Plan-Review-Permits-and-Inspections/Quick-Permits) nor DBC ADMIN 133 (https://www.denvergov.org/files/assets/public/v/5/community-planning-and-development/documents/ds/building-codes/policies/admin-133-electrical-plan-review-required.pdf) explicitly states whether a single-family residential standby generator or generator inlet with transfer switch/interlock qualifies as a Quick Permit (under 'Any other equipment or appliance with a rated voltage of over 50 volts' on services 400A or less) or requires electrical plan review; confirm with Denver CPD.

Denver's Quick Permits webpage (https://www.denvergov.org/quickpermits) and page 4+ of ADMIN 131A (https://denvergov.org/files/assets/public/v/6/community-planning-and-development/documents/ds/building-codes/policies/admin-131a.pdf) listing exact residential electrical Quick Permit scopes (EV charger, service upgrade, subpanel, appliance circuit, standalone generator) were not fully returned in search snippets; open directly to confirm exact eligibility.

Confirm the exact effective date of Denver's adoption of the 2026 NEC / NFPA 70 on https://www.denvergov.org/Government/Agencies-Departments-Offices/Agencies-Departments-Offices-Directory/Community-Planning-and-Development/Building-Codes-Policies-and-Guides.

No Denver-specific residential electrical load calculation worksheet or EV charger load factor was found on denvergov.org; confirm whether CPD requires a specific NEC 220 method for single-family electrical permits.

checklist.title: Solar Permits for Photovoltaic and Hot Water Panels

requirements.item: For SolarAPP+, upload unique SolarAPP+ ID number and approval documents under Quick Permits > Electrical Permit
requirements.quote: If your project is approved, you will receive a unique SolarAPP+ ID number and approval documents. Gather your ID number and approval documents and log in to e-permits.

requirements.item: Non-SolarAPP+ systems <10 kW require review of non-engineered electrical plans via Building Log
requirements.quote: Systems rated under 10 kW will not require engineered electrical plans, but do still require a review of non-engineered electrical plans.

requirements.item: Non-SolarAPP+ systems >=10 kW require stamped and signed engineered electrical plans via Building Log
requirements.quote: For systems 10 kW in size and over, stamped and signed(PDF, 1023KB), engineered plans must be uploaded.

requirements.item: Zoning permit required if solar panels are installed on the ground
requirements.quote: A zoning permit is required if the panels will be installed on the ground or if a generator is part of the project and will be located on the ground.

sheet_requirements.copies_or_format: Electronic PDF upload via E-permits (Quick Permits for SolarAPP+, Building Log otherwise)
sheet_requirements.signature_or_stamp: Stamped and signed engineered plans required for systems 10 kW and over
sheet_requirements.quote: For systems 10 kW in size and over, stamped and signed(PDF, 1023KB), engineered plans must be uploaded.

local_rules.rule: SolarAPP+ Quick Permit limited to licensed electricians, 1-2 family, <=400A service, <10 kW DC; may include ESS, panel upgrade/derating if PV-related
local_rules.quote: Single-family and duplex homes. With utility service of 400 amps or less. kW DC rating of less than 10. Scope of work can include energy storage systems, main panel upgrades, and main panel deratings only if related to the PV system installation.
